A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show a plausible computational role of the sparse neural codes in V1, and propose an interpretable and biologically plausible attention mechanism for few-shot image generation.
we propose a memory-based attention mechanism for image generation that can learn prototype concepts from the data, which can improve image quality, robustness and interpretability.

our proposed MoCA mechanism can be viewed as a memory-attention mechanism that can learn to bias and focus the image generation process, and can be used to model prototype concept memory in the visual cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain's memory and attention mechanisms are tightly coupled and work together to bias and shape distributed representations of visual concepts.
prototype memory can be a useful tool to improve the quality of image synthesis and can be a useful prior to guide the attention mechanism.
having prototype memory can improve the robustness and quality of few shot image generation, and can also implicitly modify self-attention in GANs.
